newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel approves shareholder bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel approves shareholder bill.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Senate approved Thursday a bill which changes existing legislation on shareholders rights and helps pave the way for privatization of power and telecommunications companies.
The Senate's Economic Affairs Committee approved the so-called Limited Companies Law with only one vote against, an offifial said.
The bill now advances to the floor of the upper house.

The legislation is considered important for upcoming privatizations because it would scrap existing rights of minority shareholders to sell their shares at above market prices should a company be split into several units.
The government is expected to split at least two of four power generating companies owned by federal electricity holding Eletrobras prior to privatization later this year or in early 1998.
The bill maintains minority shareholders' rights to sell their shares in the case of mergers.
The privatization of Brazil's telecommunications system will involve the grouping of state-level units of federally owned Telebras, probably into four regional units.
The bill approved Thursday in the Senate panel also states that holders of non-voting shares are entitled to dividends ten percent higher than those holding voting shares.
